## Biological Interpretation

The metabolite list is overwhelmingly enriched for **tryptophan metabolism** (KEGG map00380; FDR ≈ 0, fold-enrichment ≈ 584), which is by far the dominant signal. Seven of the twelve differentially-abundant metabolites map directly onto this pathway: L-tryptophan, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, and melatonin.

### Key Driver Compounds

**L-Tryptophan (C00078)** is the entry-point driver. KEGG reaction-graph traversal confirms it is the metabolic precursor of the serotonin–melatonin axis: L-tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin (4-hop forward path). This canonical route passes through tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde as verified intermediates within the tryptophan metabolism pathway, linking all three neuroactive metabolites in a single directional module. **3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632)** anchors a branch of tryptophan metabolism leading to NAD⁺ precursors, confirmed downstream of L-tryptophan via a 4-hop path, and is annotated in NAD⁺ biosynthetic pathways (WP3645 / WP2485). **Quinolinic acid (C03722)** occupies the same segment of nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG map00760) but was not reachable from L-tryptophan within the 6-hop BFS budget, suggesting it may branch through an intermediate not captured in this differential list. **Acetylcholine (C01996)** is present in the input list but its contribution to a ranked pathway is not independently supported by the top enrichment results.

### Biological Significance

L-Tryptophan serves as the shared entry point for the observed metabolites, several of which are neuroactive. Enhanced levels of serotonin and melatonin, alongside their immediate precursors indoleacetaldehyde and tryptamine, indicate stimulation of the serotonin–melatonin branch of tryptophan metabolism, consistent with known roles in mood and circadian regulation. Elevated 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid suggests activation of an oxidative arm of tryptophan degradation. **2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1** (C19586) — a mycotoxin reactive intermediate — was also detected.

### Limitations

Several biological interpretation claims (dual activation of opposing tryptophan branches, kynurenine pathway pro-oxidant/neurotoxic properties, xenobiotic trigger hypothesis) were unsupported by the pathway databases queried and have been removed or qualified. They remain plausible biological hypotheses that would require literature validation.
